analysis.title: Taiwan: Surprise Strength Extends into Q3 GDP; Revising Up 2026-27 Growth Forecasts
key_insights: Taiwan Q3 2026 real GDP grew 3.2% qoq sa (non-annualized), accelerating from 1.4% in Q2 and well above both the GS forecast and the Bloomberg consensus.
Year-on-year growth was 14.4% in Q3 versus 12.9% in Q2. GS and Bloomberg consensus both expected 12.0%.
Investment drove the acceleration, rising 8.4% qoq sa, the strongest momentum since Q2 2024. This explains most of the upside surprise versus the GS forecast.
The advance release has no breakdown of fixed investment and inventories. The DGBAS press release cited broad strength across machinery, transport equipment and intellectual property investment.
Private consumption rose 0.4% qoq sa, slowing from a 1% to 2% qoq pace in each of the previous three quarters. Government consumption rose 1.8% qoq sa, up from 1.1%.
Net exports contributed -0.1pp to headline growth, a smaller drag than -0.7pp in Q2. Exports rose 0.6% qoq sa and imports rose 1.0%.
GS raised its Taiwan real GDP growth forecasts to 13.0% for 2026 and 6.3% for 2027, from 11.7% and 3.3%. Bloomberg consensus is 11.4% and 5.1%.
The earlier upgrade focused on exports. The Q3 data suggest strength has extended to domestic demand.
For 2027, GS expects net exports to add about 4.0pp to GDP growth, with the remaining 2.3pp from private consumption and capex/R&D spending.

GS expects the tech sector's contribution to real GVA growth to ease from 6.8pp in 2026 to 4.5pp in 2027. Hyperscaler capex growth is seen slowing from over 95% yoy in 2026 to more than 40% in 2027 on consensus forecasts.

Private consumption support in 2027 includes TWD 235.7bn (about $7.4bn, 0.7% of GDP) in universal cash handouts, with the first tranche due in late January 2027. Other supports are a 4% public-sector wage increase, bonuses from leading tech firms and equity wealth effects.

Gross fixed capital formation is expected to grow around 5% in 2027. AI-related capex is projected to add 7.0pp to fixed investment growth as TSMC expands advanced and packaging capacity. Non-tech fixed investment, notably construction, is expected to pull back as property cools.

sector_views.rationale: Tech manufacturing is expected to stay strong in 2027 on global AI demand and rising hyperscaler capex expectations. Tech's contribution to GVA growth is forecast at 4.5pp.

Non-tech fixed investment, notably construction, is expected to pull back after three years of gains. Residential and commercial property is cooling and construction starts have trended down since the mid-2024 peak.
